- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast peak at 1–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model often fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for 2–3 periods.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 1–3%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; use 14-day average as baseline, then adjust ±1–2% based on sentiment momentum.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is flat, model tends to drift upward; apply downward correction of 0.5–1.0% to avoid false breakout.
